newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Henderson Land interims beat forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Henderson Land interims beat forecasts.

text.p: Henderson Land Development Co Ltd beat market expectations for interim earnings growth on Wednesday by posting a 33 percent rise in net profit.

The Hong Kong property developer, one of the most profitable in the territory, said net profit for the six months to December 31, 1996, rose to HK$5.32 billion compared with HK$4.01 billion in the same period the previous year.
Turnover rose to HK$10.30 billion compared with HK$6.84 billion.

"During the period under review, the local property market gathered much momentum. Residential properties registered a substantial price increase and residential property sales activities also increased substantially," Henderson Land said in a statement.
"Barring unforeseen circumstances, the group's results for the current financial year are anticipated to show steady growth as compared to those recorded in the previous financial year," it added.
Henderson Land said the completion of relatively large development projects, including its Tolo Place and Metro City developments in the New Territories, had contributed to the sharp rise in profits.
"Overall the results were better than expected," said Desmond Cheung, an analyst at Vickers Ballas.
He had expected interim net profit HK$4.5 billion and said he was revising up his full year forecast to HK$11.6 billion from a current HK$11.3 billion.
Henderson Land reported net profit for the year to June 30, 1996, of HK$8.36 billion.
Adrian Ngan, a director at Peregrine Securities, said the booking of Metro City profits had led to the better than expected interim results.
"Metro City was the marginal case. It looks like they booked some of the profit from Metro City in the first half. That is why they are a bit better than expected," he said.
Ngan had forecast interim net profit of HK$4.2 billion but said he would probably maintain his full-year forecast at around HK$10 billion.
Henderson Land's 64.27 percent-owned unit Henderson Investment Ltd unit posted interim net profit of HK$898.21 million compared with HK$1.34 billion.
"As there was no development project completed during the period under review, the net profit decreased by 33 percent," Henderson Investment said in a statement.
Ngan said the results were better than expected.
He had forecast first-half net profit of only HK$600 million and said he was likely to revise his full year estimate to slightly more than HK$2.1 billion from a current forecast of HK$1.9 billion.
Henderson Investment, which joined the blue chip Hang Seng Index in August 1996, posted net profit for the year to June 30, 1996 of HK$1.89 billion.
Henderson China Holdings Ltd, a spinoff of Henderson Land, reported net profit for the six months to December 31, 1996, of HK$163.96 million compared with HK$11.71 million.
